page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with x86_64 architecture, offering 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 1800 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores both ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering strong read-only performance for both small cached blocks (3706.44 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (209.03 GB/sec). Database operations and Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance, with Redis achieving 61.64 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are relatively weaker, with LLM text generation for a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5d.18xlarge delivers high compute density and high-speed local NVMe storage, which eliminates the need for external block storage for temporary data. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for compute-heavy workloads that require fast local scratch space. Appropriate workloads include high-performance database operations, multi-threaded data processing, batch computing, and web serving, though it is less suited for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM text generation.
